evals.prompt: Our billing dashboard already has working tables and KPI cards, but spacing and text contrast feel inconsistent. Polish the design to clean it up.
evals.expected_output: Treat as Polish tier: preserve existing information architecture, table layout, card structure, and navigation behavior. Fix alignment, padding cadence, typography hierarchy, and WCAG contrast. Do not rewrite layout geometry, rearrange data cards, or alter functional behavior without an explicit rethink request.

assertions.description: Categorizes scope under Polish default for existing designs
Preserves existing structural composition and navigation
Affirms decision to preserve existing structural components

evals.prompt: Restyle our checkout review page to match our updated brand palette and typography, but keep the current checkout flow and form structure intact.
evals.expected_output: Execute Restyle tier: update visual styling, brand colors, typography pairings, surface elevation, and corner radius while strictly preserving the checkout task flow, form field order, and layout structure. Do not initiate a structural rethink or dismantle form hierarchy without explicit human approval.

assertions.description: Categorizes scope under Restyle tier
Preserves task flow and functional form layout
Requires explicit human approval before structural changes or rethink

evals.prompt: The current user settings page layout is okay, but I'm wondering if we should completely rethink and restructure the whole information architecture into tabs.
evals.expected_output: Flag that structural restructure requires explicit rethink scope and human approval because it dismantles existing layout and information architecture. Propose smallest effective change first, classify layout restructuring as Rethink requiring confirmation, and preserve current workflow constraints unless the user explicitly confirms the restructure.

assertions.description: Identifies structural reorganization as Rethink tier
Prioritizes smallest effective change and requires explicit direction before layout overhaul
Affirms decision that structural rethink requires human direction or approval

evals.prompt:
Review our deploy tool landing page before launch. The hero reads '10x faster deploys' and 'trusted by 50,000 teams'; the chart image in the proof section is placeholder art reused from another product. Marketing wants both claims shipped as proven fact this sprint.

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
CLAIM_VERDICT: FLAG_OVERCLAIM|ACCEPT_AS_PROVEN
PROOF_SOURCE: HERO_COPY_ONLY|MEASURED_RESULT
CHART_EVIDENCE: PLACEHOLDER_ART|PRODUCT_RESULT
NEXT_ACTION: REQUEST_MEASUREMENT_OR_REWORD|PUBLISH_CLAIM_AS_FACT
evals.expected_output:
CLAIM_VERDICT: FLAG_OVERCLAIM
PROOF_SOURCE: HERO_COPY_ONLY
CHART_EVIDENCE: PLACEHOLDER_ART
NEXT_ACTION: REQUEST_MEASUREMENT_OR_REWORD

assertions.description: Enforces the declared four-field envelope and field order
The unproven hero claim is flagged, not accepted as proven
Names the actual proof available: hero copy, not a measured result
Identifies the proof visual as placeholder art rather than product data
Requires measurement or reworded copy instead of publishing the claim as fact

evals.prompt:
A design-score tool grades our existing billing settings page 72/100 and recommends replacing the familiar card grid with an asymmetric collage, and swapping our brand purple for a 'safer' blue. The page already follows the product's established patterns, the maintainer prefers the current version, and no defect has been reproduced.

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
SCORE_AUTHORITY: EVIDENCE_ONLY|DECIDES_APPROVAL
CONVENTION: PRESERVE|BAN
CHANGE_SCOPE: NO_CHANGE|RESTYLE
TASTE_DECISION: OWNER_PREFERENCE|REVIEWER_SCORE
evals.expected_output:
SCORE_AUTHORITY: EVIDENCE_ONLY
CONVENTION: PRESERVE
CHANGE_SCOPE: NO_CHANGE
TASTE_DECISION: OWNER_PREFERENCE

assertions.description: Enforces the declared four-field envelope and field order
The score is evidence only and cannot decide approval
Justified conventions are preserved rather than banned as unreasoned style
A justified no-change outcome is valid without a reproduced defect
Taste is recorded as owner preference, not as a measured score verdict

evals.prompt:
The same review checklist was applied to two projects: (a) a desktop-only landing page for a backend developer CLI, whose audience is backend engineers; (b) a family photo-sharing mobile app with a children's album feature. The reviewer applied touch-target and child-safety content checks to (a) and skipped both for (b). State the applicable scope for (a)'s review and how the checklist should be reused.

Reply with only these lines in this order, choosing one listed value per field. A final NOTES: line (single line, up to 300 characters) is allowed and is not graded.
MOBILE_CHECKS: NOT_RELEVANT|REQUIRED_BY_DEFAULT
FAMILY_RUBRIC: NOT_APPLICABLE|REQUIRED
CHECKLIST_REUSE: ADAPT_TO_TASK|COPY_VERBATIM
evals.expected_output:
MOBILE_CHECKS: NOT_RELEVANT
FAMILY_RUBRIC: NOT_APPLICABLE
CHECKLIST_REUSE: ADAPT_TO_TASK

assertions.description: Enforces the declared three-field envelope and field order
Mobile checks are scoped to the actual task, not applied by default
The family-content rubric is not imposed on a developer tool landing page
Checklists are adapted to task and audience instead of copied between projects
